title: Hydra TPS Explorer: microbenchmark harness for tokens/sec stability and regression bisecting
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Our core models have shown occasional p95 regressions under microburst and sustained load. Existing microbench suites cover many token-rate profiles but lack an integrated bisect-friendly harness that can run staggered microbursts, capture per-request p95 and tail histograms, and produce a deterministic fingerprint for regression triage.

Goal: Build and maintain a reusable tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness (Hydra TPS Explorer) that can: 1) generate configurable traffic shapes (steady, burst, ramp, mixed), 2) measure per-request latency, CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates, 3) compute p50/p90/p95/p99 across sliding windows, 4) emit fingerprints and digests to enable automatic regression bisecting, and 5) integrate with CI, dashboards and the regression-detector alerting pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run 10+ concurrent user profiles and generate 0.1-10k tokens/sec per profile with reproducible configs
Output JSON lines include timestamped per-request latencies, model-version, kernel-config, KV cache utilization, sequence-length distribution and a deterministic run-fingerprint
CI job exists that runs a smoke battery against core-models nightly and fails when p95 regression > 10% compared to baseline
Dashboards display sliding-window p95 trends and allow drilldown from a regression alert to the run fingerprint and associated PRs
Bisect workflow documented so SREs can reproduce and attach artifacts to a regression triage ticket
tasks: Design run config schema and traffic shape DSL (support burst/ramp/multi-cohort)
Implement runner with pluggable load generators and per-request tracing hooks
Add KV cache instrumentation and compute cache-hit adjusted latency
Produce deterministic fingerprint generator (inputs: model, weights-hash, kernel selection, batch-size, seed, config)
CI: nightly job + PR gate integration + regression detector hook
Dashboard: Grafana panels + links from alerts to run artifacts
Write runbook and bisect playbook for oncall and SRE
proposed_solution: Implement a Python-based orchestrator that spins up synthetic traffic workers (asyncio) and a light C++ extension for precise token emission timing. Use protobuf v3 for compact line-delimited output and include an SHA256 run-fingerprint. Persist artifacts to s3 with a stable prefix and push summary metrics to Prometheus for dashboarding. Integrate with existing regression-detector (ENG-9421) and the CI orchestration used by throughput-sentinel jobs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Load generator skew and jitter causing noisy p95s -> Mitigation: include client-side synchronized timebase and hardware timestamp where available
Risk: Overfitting to our internal cluster topology -> Mitigation: test on dedicated and hosted stacks, and include variability in kernel selection
Risk: High storage of detailed traces -> Mitigation: compress line-delimited protobuf and retain artifacts for 30 days behind lifecycle policy
